{{Short description|Equation for function that computes iterated values}}
{{hatnote|This article is about certain functional equations.  For ordinary differential equations which are cubic in the unknown function, see [[Abel equation of the first kind]].}}

The '''Abel equation''', named after [[Niels Henrik Abel]], is a type of [[functional equation]] of the form
:<math>f(h(x)) = h(x + 1)</math>
or
:<math>\alpha(f(x)) = \alpha(x)+1</math>.
The forms are equivalent when {{mvar|α}} is [[invertible function|invertible]]. {{mvar|h}} or {{mvar|α}} control the [[iterated function|iteration]] of {{mvar|f}}.

==Equivalence==
The second equation can be written
:<math>\alpha^{-1}(\alpha(f(x))) = \alpha^{-1}(\alpha(x)+1)\, .</math>

Taking {{math|''x'' {{=}} ''α''<sup>−1</sup>(''y'')}}, the equation can be written
::<math>f(\alpha^{-1}(y)) = \alpha^{-1}(y+1)\, .</math>

For a known function {{math|''f''(''x'')}} , a problem is to solve the functional equation for the function {{math|''α''<sup>−1</sup> ≡ ''h''}}, possibly satisfying additional requirements, such as {{math|''α''<sup>−1</sup>(0)&nbsp;{{=}}&nbsp;1}}.

The change of variables {{math|''s''<sup>''α''(''x'')</sup> {{=}}  Ψ(''x'')}}, for a [[real number|real]] parameter {{mvar|s}}, brings Abel's equation into the celebrated [[Schröder's equation]], {{math|Ψ(''f''(''x'')) {{=}} ''s''&nbsp;Ψ(''x'')}} .

The further change {{math|''F''(''x'') {{=}} exp(''s''<sup>''α''(''x'')</sup>)}} into [[Böttcher's equation]], {{math|''F''(''f''(''x'')) {{=}} ''F''(''x'')<sup>''s''</sup>}}.

The Abel equation is a special case of (and easily generalizes to) the '''translation equation''',<ref>[[János Aczél (mathematician)|Aczél, János]], (1966): ''Lectures on Functional Equations and Their Applications'', [[Academic Press]],  reprinted by Dover Publications,  {{ISBN|0486445232}} .</ref>
:<math>\omega( \omega(x,u),v)=\omega(x,u+v) ~,</math>
e.g., for <math>\omega(x,1) = f(x)</math>, 
:<math>\omega(x,u) = \alpha^{-1}(\alpha(x)+u)</math>. &nbsp; &nbsp; (Observe {{math|''ω''(''x'',0) {{=}} ''x''}}.) 

The Abel function {{math|''α''(''x'')}} further provides the canonical coordinate for [[Shift operator|Lie advective flows]] (one parameter [[Lie group]]s).

{{see also|Iterated function#Abelian property and Iteration sequences}}

==Special cases==

The equation of [[tetration]] is a special case of Abel's equation, with {{math|''f'' {{=}} exp}}.

In the case of an integer argument, the equation encodes  a recurrent procedure, e.g.,
:<math>\alpha(f(f(x)))=\alpha(x)+2 ~,</math>
and so on,
:<math>\alpha(f_n(x))=\alpha(x)+n ~.</math>

==Solutions==
The Abel equation has at least one solution on <math>E</math> [[if and only if]] for all <math>x \in E</math> and all <math>n \in \mathbb{N}^*</math>, <math>f^{n}(x) \neq x</math>, where <math> f^{n} = f \circ f \circ ... \circ f</math>, is the function {{mvar|f}} [[iterated function|iterated]] {{mvar|n}} times.<ref>[http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm5/fm5132.pdf R. Tambs Lyche, Sur l'équation fonctionnelle d'Abel, University of Trondlyim, Norvege]</ref>

We have the following existence and uniqueness theorem<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bonet |first=José |last2=Domański |first2=Paweł |date=April 2015 |title=Abel’s Functional Equation and Eigenvalues of Composition Operators on Spaces of Real Analytic Functions |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00020-014-2175-4 |journal=Integral Equations and Operator Theory |language=en |volume=81 |issue=4 |pages=455–482 |doi=10.1007/s00020-014-2175-4 |issn=0378-620X|doi-access=free |hdl=10251/71248 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>{{Pg|location=Theorem B}}

Let <math>h: \R \to \R</math> be [[Analytic function|analytic]], meaning it has a Taylor expansion. To find: real analytic solutions <math>\alpha: \R \to \C</math> of the Abel equation <math display="inline">\alpha \circ h = \alpha + 1</math>.

=== Existence ===

A real analytic solution <math>\alpha</math> exists if and only if both of the following conditions hold:

* <math>h</math> has no [[Fixed point (mathematics)|fixed points]], meaning there is no <math>y \in \R</math> such that <math>h(y) = y</math>.
* The set of [[Critical point (mathematics)|critical points]] of <math>h</math>, where <math>h'(y) = 0</math>, is bounded above if <math>h(y) > y </math> for all <math>y</math>, or bounded below if <math>h(y) < y</math> for all <math>y</math>.

=== Uniqueness ===

The solution is essentially unique in the sense that there exists a canonical solution <math>\alpha_0</math> with the following properties:

* The set of critical points of <math>\alpha_0</math> is bounded above if <math>h(y) > y </math> for all <math>y</math>, or bounded below if <math>h(y) < y</math> for all <math>y</math>.
* This canonical solution generates all other solutions. Specifically, the set of all real analytic solutions is given by

<math display=block>
\{\alpha_0 + \beta\circ \alpha_0 | \beta : \R \to \R \text{ is analytic, with period 1}\}.
</math>

=== Approximate solution ===
Analytic solutions (Fatou coordinates) can be approximated by [[asymptotic expansion]] of a function defined by [[power series]] in the sectors around a [[Classification of Fatou components|parabolic fixed point]].<ref>Dudko, Artem (2012). [http://www.math.toronto.edu/graduate/Dudko-thesis.pdf  ''Dynamics of holomorphic maps: Resurgence of Fatou coordinates, and Poly-time computability of Julia sets''] Ph.D. Thesis</ref> The analytic solution is unique up to a constant.<ref>[https://www.birs.ca/workshops/2015/15w5082/files/resman.pdf Classifications of parabolic germs and fractal properties of orbits by Maja Resman, University of Zagreb, Croatia]</ref>
